SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Headline

The Seller's package is a one-sided markup framed as "negotiated positions". Nothing in it has been agreed by us. Three structural features matter most:

1. **A hidden override.** The proposal to apply "any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), together with cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, would pull title, capacity, tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud into the general regime.
2. **Wide deemed disclosure and buyer-knowledge exclusions** (Sch 7, cl 8.3, DL 1.1-1.2). These could strip most warranty protection.
3. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note** on Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and the incident.

Two Seller numbers (20% / AUD 4.8M cap and 18 months) match our fallbacks. That does not clear them. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for either, and the authority must identify the specific draft.

## Departures from our playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our position | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | 25% / AUD 6M. The 20% fallback needs Frost's written authority, which has not been given. | Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6M. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject on both amount and mechanism. |
| Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Frost's written approval, which has not been given. | Reject. Counter at 24 months. |
| Blanket limitations (12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Separate regimes by category. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. | Reject. Insert carve-outs. Nobody on our side can waive the fraud carve-out. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cut title protection. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1-1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject all deemed and general disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete. Any qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | Delete. "Discoverable" imports constructive knowledge, which is worse than actual knowledge. |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery. | Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied, before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. | Reject. See below. |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval, which has not been given. | Reject. |
| Bonuses | "Matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Specific line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs | Reject the silent exclusion. |
| Ironquay (11.1) | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment | Broaden it and preserve the SOW3 cure | Reject. |
| Incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Preliminary, not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. | Reject the characterisation. |
| Sandbar | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | Neither accept nor concede. Diligence first. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open. No assumed outcome. Separate categories. | Reject. Say expressly that they are not settled. |
| Title | DD-012 register is the evidence | Independent evidence required. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | Reject as sufficient. |

## Reasoning on the key issues

**1. Caps, thresholds and time limits.**
- The Seller's package moves every dial at once: lower cap, a 5x de minimis, a 5x basket that is also a deductible, and a shorter period. The deductible basket means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is never recoverable. Combined with a AUD 25,000 de minimis, many individually small but collectively real warranty losses would fall out entirely.
- The cover note's "key negotiated positions" wording risks creating an impression of concession. Our reply should say that no position is agreed until the full agreement is settled.
- Do not reveal our fallbacks. If the deal team wants to consider 20% or 18 months, the right step is a request to Amelia Frost for written authority identifying the specific draft. Even then, only conditionally and as a trade for something else.

**2. Limitation provisions overriding every category.**
- "Applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" inverts the structure we want. Our approach is to keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims in separate regimes, with no hidden general-regime override.
- Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, as drafted, would also apply exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses to fraud. Exclusion of fraud may be unenforceable in any event. Our position is a carve-out "to the maximum extent enforceable", which should be stated in the draft.
- Specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, any incident indemnity) must also sit outside the general cap, basket and time limits.

**3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.**
- DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room, and 1.2 adds public records. Combined with cl 8.3, the Buyer would have almost no warranty claim for anything findable.
- We want specific fair disclosure against identified warranties.
- The data room cut-off is **5.00pm 22 September 2026**. Today is 6 November 2026, so the facts are over six weeks stale. Require a refreshed data room index and a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter. This particularly affects the incident, Bluefen, Riverlark and the Ironquay payment status.
- DL 1.4 (no admission of breach, materiality or legal requirement) is acceptable as a non-admission. It must not be read as limiting warranties or indemnities.

**4. Bluefen (about AUD 3.6M, about 30% of FY26 revenue).**
- The cover note says the consent is "addressed". DL 2 says there is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The two documents contradict each other.
- Because this is a material customer, reasonable endeavours is inadequate. A consent that is "satisfied on delivery" could be delivered subject to unmet conditions.
- Require a condition precedent: written consent effective in accordance with its terms, plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are met, before Completion. Review the consent's wording once received.

**5. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2M).**
- DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. A post-Completion release leaves security over the Company with the buyer holding the risk. It also conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free basis of the AUD 24M price.
- Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases (including PPSR and any share or other security) on Completion. A post-completion release is available only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Frost approval, neither of which exists.

**6. Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).**
- Both the Seller update and DL 5 confirm the bonuses are not in the funds flow. The statement that the funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics" is not accepted.
- Because they are triggered by Completion, the Company, and so the Buyer, would bear them unless they are funded.
- DL 5 does not say whether payroll tax, super or other on-costs apply. Ask the Seller to quantify them and require either a specific line item in the funds flow or Seller funding by price deduction or direct payment.

**7. Ironquay.**
- DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but DL 4 concedes this is not independent verification, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists.
- We should not assert the amount is unpaid or owed. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's view that a narrow payment indemnity is adequate.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses from the Ironquay matter generally, including IP ownership, licence, claims and costs. Preserve the SOW3 cure (payment, then assignment of the Project Materials). Request bank evidence of payment status and the confirmatory assignment.

**8. DD-006 export incident.**
- "Preliminary, not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation. DL 6 itself says scope, access and notification are undetermined (about 1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and timestamps).
- We should not call it a breach, and we should not accept it as immaterial. Require:
  - preservation of logs;
  - a prompt investigation with the findings shared;
  - regular updates and cooperation;
  - a covenant to consult us before any regulator or individual notification (where lawfully possible);
  - a warranty or indemnity position that is not neutralised by general disclosure.
- Put no number on loss in either direction.

**9. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate, three at AUD 110,000).**
- DL 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The Seller's "ordinary-course" label is therefore unsupported.
- Request the contracts (DD-008, DD-011), termination and notice rights, and accrual treatment. Only then decide whether any price or working-capital treatment is warranted. Do not classify them as Debt or deduct from price at this stage.

**10. Tax and IP.**
- The Seller treats these as "settled under the general regime". They are open for us. Say so in writing. Do not suggest we have accepted, or are demanding, unlimited liability. Keep separate Tax and IP regimes in the mark-up.

**11. Title.**
- The only title evidence is the Seller-supplied register at DD-012, and DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC extract;
  - the share issue and transfer history;
  - the constitution and any approvals;
  - confirmation of no encumbrances (including whether Riverlark holds share security);
  - evidence of the Seller's capacity and authority to sell.

**12. Lower-priority diligence items.**
- DL 7 (office lease, notification obligation) and DL 9 (Mossvale, assignment restriction) are described as not requiring consent merely on a share sale. Confirm this from the underlying documents and diarise the lease notification, rather than relying on the Disclosure Letter's wording.

## Recommendations

**Pushback in the mark-up**
1. Counter at 25% / AUD 6M cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, and 24 months. Do not indicate that 20% or 18 months are acceptable.
2. Delete the "all Claims" language in 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5. Add the fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out, and a separate Title/Fundamental regime (100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge).
3. Replace Schedule 7 and DL 1.1-1.2 with specific fair disclosure. Delete cl 8.3 or replace it with a narrow named-person, reasonable-enquiry qualifier that never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
4. Draft CPs and Completion deliverables for Bluefen (effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions) and Riverlark (payout, direct repayment from funds, releases).
5. Require the DD-005 bonuses and on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded.
6. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
7. Add incident covenants (preservation, investigation, updates) and reject the "not material" characterisation.
8. State that Tax and IP remain open and are not settled.

**Information requests**
- Refreshed data room index and bring-down of the Disclosure Letter (the cut-off of 22 September is stale).
- Bluefen consent drafts and the 11.3 conditions evidence.
- A Riverlark payout letter and draft security releases.
- Bonus on-cost calculations.
- Ironquay payment evidence and a draft confirmatory assignment.
- Incident logs and investigation updates.
- Sandbar contracts and accrual information.
- Independent title and encumbrance evidence.

**Internal actions**
- If the deal team wants any flexibility on the cap or claims period, ask Amelia Frost for written authority that identifies the specific draft. We do not currently have it and should not signal flexibility without it.
- Reply to Seller's counsel that none of the Seller's positions is agreed, that the Disclosure Letter's own admissions contradict the cover note, and that our full mark-up will follow.
- Treat the Seller's phrases ("agreed price mechanics", "adequate", "settled", "considered not material") as assertions, not verified facts.
